claims.text: The baseline HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase alloy.
Rapid quenching maintains a disordered atomic arrangement in HfNbTaTiZr.
Subsolidus annealing at 600–800°C induces short-range chemical order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing at 600–800°C can induce short-range order without macroscopic phase segregation.
Chemical complexity and local stoichiometric deviations can give rise to local chemical short-range order in concentrated alloys including HfNbTaTiZr.
The degree of short-range atomic order can be quantitatively represented by an experimentally measured order parameter.
Short-range order reduces random local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order alters local bond stiffness in HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced lattice-distortion randomness diminishes anharmonic phonon scattering.
Diminished anharmonic phonon scattering leads to a lower thermal-expansion coefficient.
Short-range-order-induced changes in bonding increase the effective elastic stiffness at elevated temperatures.
Annealed, short-range-ordered specimens will have a lower thermal-expansion coefficient above 700°C than rapidly quenched specimens.
Annealed, short-range-ordered specimens will have a higher elastic modulus above 700°C than rapidly quenched specimens.
Rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr has more atomic disorder than the annealed state.
Greater atomic disorder causes higher thermal expansion and lower elastic modulus at elevated temperatures.
Phonon and anharmonic contributions are significant in HfNbTaTiZr between approximately 700°C and 1000°C.
HfNbTaTiZr remains free of phase segregation or macroscopic transformations over the proposed 700–1000°C test range.
